# s452 — check: a backtick slicer command ends at the first shell operator

`slicer check` parses each backticked `slicer ...` span in a live slice and reports flags the parser rejects. It reads every token after `slicer` as that command's words, so a span that chains commands with `&&`, `||`, `;` or `|` makes the words of the next command look like unknown flags. Cut the tokens at the first shell control operator; check each `slicer` command in the span on its own.

**Findings:** Found from ork, 2026-11-05 (ork friction F48, while promoting ork S280): a Why section held the backticked text slicer goals --json --lean && echo '---LIST---' && ... (quoting a command a Grok role ran). slicer check failed with 'S280 / Why: unknown flag ---LIST--- in ...'. Fact: _slice_flag_problems (src/slicer/cli_common.py:550-585) shlex-splits the whole span and passes every token after 'slicer' to the parser, so the tokens after && (echo and its argument) are read as flags of the slicer command. Needed: cut the tokens at the first shell control operator (&&, ||, ;, |) before parsing, so only the slicer command's own words are checked; a later slicer command in the same span after the operator may be checked on its own. Test: a slice whose section holds that span passes check, and slicer goals --bogus && echo x still reports --bogus. Related: S116, s183. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-07** — Verified: a backticked slicer command in a live slice now ends at the first shell operator (&&, ||, ;, |); each slicer command in the span is checked on its own, and an unknown flag before the operator is still reported. Lexer keeps # as an ordinary character like shlex.split. Full suite 3234 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped; slicer check passes.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** pipes, redirections or subshells beyond cutting at the operator; spans that do not start with `slicer ` (for example `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer ...`), which stay unchecked as today; running any command.

## Why

Found from ork, 2026-11-05 (ork friction F48, while promoting ork S280): a Why section held, in backticks, a command a Grok role ran (shown here in a fence, which `check` skips, because this slice's own Why would otherwise trip the bug):

```
slicer goals --json --lean && echo '---LIST---' && ...
```

`slicer check` failed with `S280 / Why: unknown flag ---LIST--- in ...`.

What the code shows (read 2026-11-06): `_slice_flag_problems` (`src/slicer/cli_common.py:551-587`) takes each backtick span outside fences, keeps it when it starts with `slicer `, runs `shlex.split(command)` (`:579`) and passes `tokens[1:]` to `_unknown_flags` (`:533-548`), which returns the extras of `parse_known_args` that start with `-`. Nothing stops at `&&`, so `echo` and `---LIST---` reach the parser. Plain `shlex.split` also keeps an operator glued to a word (`--lean&&echo` is one token); `shlex.shlex(command, posix=True, punctuation_chars=True)` splits operators out as their own tokens (stdlib).

Related: S116 (the flag check), s183.

## Implement

1. Tests first; confirm each fails (or the guard passes) for the reason given.
2. In `_slice_flag_problems`, tokenize with `shlex.shlex(command, posix=True, punctuation_chars=True)` and `whitespace_split=True`; on `ValueError` skip the span as today.
3. Split the token list into commands at tokens that are exactly one of `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` (with `punctuation_chars`, also treat a token made only of those characters, such as `;;` or `|&`, as a cut). For each command whose first token is `slicer`, run `_unknown_flags(parser, tokens[1:])`.
4. Keep the problem text as today: `ID / Section: unknown flag FLAG in `SPAN``, quoting the whole span so a person can find it.
5. Update the docstring of `_slice_flag_problems` (one sentence on the cut) and add the CHANGELOG line.
